LESSON: WRITING 8.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: FILLING FORMS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we fill forms?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify parts of a simple form for information
2. create a form related to the theme
3. appreciate value of forms for giving information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 8.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: FILLING FORMS
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 8.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: FILLING FORMS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify parts of a simple form for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify parts of a simple form for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify parts of a simple form for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify parts of a simple form for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a form related to the theme

What this means
In this part you learn to create a form related to the theme. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a form related to the theme.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a form related to the theme. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate value of forms for giving information

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate value of forms for giving information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate value of forms for giving information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate value of forms for giving information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify parts of a simple form for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms to a partner. (skill: create a form related to the theme)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate value of forms for giving information)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify parts of a simple form for information.
3. Practise this skill: create a form related to the theme.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate value of forms for giving information.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we fill forms?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify parts of a simple form for information.
5. Be able to: create a form related to the theme.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
